Definition: properly, to bore, i.e. (by implication) to wound, to dissolve; figuratively, to profane (a person, place or thing), to break (one's word), to begin (as if by an 'opening wedge'); to play (the flute)
BiblicalUsage: Chalal means to begin — and to profane, to wound, to dissolve. Then began men to call upon the name of the LORD, the altar of hewn stone is polluted if a tool is lifted on it, the name of God must not be profaned by Molech, and Moses told Aaron the plague is begun among the people.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe beginning and profaning share one word because every beginning is a risk: men began to call on God, and men began to profane Him. The same root holds the first prayer and the first pollution.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
